answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable deposit before transacting, slashed when peers attest to a fake identity. Like a jetty forcing boats through one narrow channel, the deposit is a chokepoint: a thousand fake agents cost a thousand deposits, and quartz-clear on-chain records tie each deposit to one funding source. Reputation grows slowly, like cedar adding rings, so a new identity cannot buy trust overnight. The attacker pays real capital per identity and waits months to look established, while honest agents keep their stake and earn fees.
